newsitem.title: USA: Benton sees $65 mln EBRD Russia loan soon.
newsitem.headline: Benton sees $65 mln EBRD Russia loan soon.

text.p: Benton Oil & Gas Co expects the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to agree a $65 million loan for the company to develop the North Gubinskoye oilfiled in Russia.

"Our people are in the final throes of negotiations about the loan and we expect to take down the first tranche in the next week or two," Alex Benton, the company's chief executive, told the Howard Weil energy conference here on Monday.
Benton said that the field was currently producing 6,000- 7,000 barrels of oil per day and had potential reserves 344 million barrels of oil and 1.9 trillion cubic feet of natural gas.
"It is becoming easier to do business in Russia. Their erratic tax regime appears to be getting less erratic," Benton said.
He said that Benton could net $5.00 per barrel of oil after costs and taxes from the North Gubinskoye field.
He sees output from the field, which is located close to both gas and oil pipelines, rising to 20,000 barrels of oil per day by the end of this year and 35,000 by end-1998.
Benton said that he expected to conclude an agreement with Russian natural gas giant RAO Gazprom to start shipping natural gas, which is currently flared off.

He said that two-thirds of daily production would be used domestically in Russia for which Benton would not receive payment and one third could be exported for which it would receive 50 cents per thousand cubic feet.
"It does not sound a lot, but it is cheap to access," Benton said.

As well as Russia, Benton Oil is involved in a discovery in the South China Sea, at the Wan'an Bei block 21, which is an area disputed by China and Vietnam, who both claim ownership of the nearby Spratly Islands.
"The area is in dispute and we are waiting for that dispute to be resolved. China and Vietnam will likely negotiate a treaty to develop commercial interests jointly," Benton said.
He added that Benton would have to seek partners for the field as it covers 7.4 million acres, and DuPont Co's Conoco subsidary was a likely partner.
In Venezuela, Benton is set to participate in the next exploration licensing round, while in the U.S. it plans to develop the Molino project in California, in which it has a 40 percent stake.
Benton said that the company has been awarded all approvals to develop Molino, which is next to the giant offshore Hondo field and adjacent to gas and oil pipelines and a Conoco processing plant.
The company will drill the first well in the fourth quarter of this year and will exploit the field using onshore rigs.
"This has potential reserves of 175 million barrels of oil and 450 billion cubic feet of gas," Benton said.
